issues.title: Softmax output is fed to CrossEntropyLoss
issues.message: SmallNet.forward returns F.softmax(x, dim=1) (model.py:33) and that value is passed as the input of nn.CrossEntropyLoss at train.py:46, so the softmax is applied twice.
issues.why: CrossEntropyLoss applies log-softmax internally; feeding it probabilities flattens the gradient and the model trains far slower or not at all.
issues.fixHint: Return the raw logits from SmallNet.forward and apply softmax only where you need probabilities for reporting.

issues.title: Gradients are never zeroed
issues.message: The batch loop at train.py:44 calls loss.backward() (line 48) and optimizer.step() (line 49) but never optimizer.zero_grad(). Gradients accumulate across batches.
issues.why: Accumulated gradients make each update the sum of all previous batches, so training diverges or converges to the wrong place - silently.
issues.fixHint: Call optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) as the first statement of the loop body, before the forward pass.

issues.title: Training DataLoader does not shuffle
issues.message: train_loader (data.py:31) wraps train_ds, the TRAIN_SPLIT half of the random_split at data.py:28, with no shuffle= and no sampler=; the batch loop at train.py:44 backprops through it.
issues.why: Batches then follow dataset order, so every epoch sees the same correlated sequence and the model can latch onto ordering instead of content.
issues.fixHint: Pass shuffle=True to the training DataLoader (or supply a shuffling sampler=).

issues.title: Evaluation loop is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
issues.message: validate() (train.py:11) runs the model over val_loader at train.py:15 with no torch.no_grad() / torch.inference_mode() block and no decorator on the function.
issues.why: Autograd keeps the graph for every evaluation batch, which wastes memory and can OOM on the validation pass even though the results stay correct.
issues.fixHint: Wrap the loop in with torch.no_grad(): (or decorate validate with @torch.no_grad()).

issues.title: Split without random_state
issues.message: train_test_split at sklearn_baseline.py:20 shuffles by default but receives no random_state=, so the train/test partition differs on every run.
issues.why: Scores from two runs are not comparable, and a lucky split cannot be told from a real improvement.
issues.fixHint: Pass random_state=42 to train_test_split so the split is reproducible independently of global RNG state.
